title: Gradable and ungradable adjectives
summary: Градуируемые (very good) и неградуируемые (absolutely fantastic) прилагательные, предельные (almost impossible), двойное quite, much/far при сравнении и коллокации.
ru:
## Градуируемые и неградуируемые
**Градуируемые** прилагательные описывают качество, которое можно измерить по шкале: *good, tired, cold, old, expensive*. К ним подходят *very, extremely, fairly, rather, quite, a bit* и сравнительная степень.
**Неградуируемые** — это три типа:
1. **Крайние (extreme):** значение уже включает «очень». *enormous* (= very big), *terrible, fantastic, exhausted, freezing, furious, delighted, brilliant, awful, hilarious, starving, tiny, ancient.*
2. **Предельные (absolute, limit):** состояние либо есть, либо нет. *perfect, impossible, essential, unique, dead, identical, unanimous, right.*
3. **Классифицирующие:** относят предмет к категории. *wooden, nuclear, medical, British, daily, electric, annual.*

## Какое усилительное слово выбрать
| Тип | Подходят | Не подходят |
|---|---|---|
| Градуируемые | very, extremely, really, fairly, pretty, rather, quite, a bit | ~~absolutely good~~ |
| Крайние / предельные | **absolutely, utterly, completely, totally, really** | ~~very exhausted~~, ~~very impossible~~ |
| Предельные (почти) | **almost, nearly, virtually, practically** | |
> The view was **absolutely breathtaking**, but I was only **very tired**.
> It is **virtually impossible** to find a parking space here. — Практически невозможно.
- ~~very fantastic~~ → **absolutely** fantastic / **really** fantastic
- ~~absolutely tired~~ → **very** tired / **absolutely exhausted**
- ~~very impossible~~ → **almost** impossible / **absolutely** impossible
**really** — универсальное слово: *really good* и *really fantastic* оба верны.

## Особая роль quite
Британский *quite* имеет **два значения**:
- с градуируемыми прилагательными = «довольно, умеренно»: *quite good* (= fairly good, не великолепно);
- с крайними и предельными = «совершенно, полностью»: *quite impossible, quite perfect, quite right.*
Американцы часто используют *quite* как *very*: *quite good* = очень хорошо. А ещё: *rather* ≈ *quite*, но обычно с оттенком неожиданности или недовольства: *rather expensive, rather good (я не ожидал)*.

## Сравнительная степень градуируемых
Усиливаем сравнительную степень словами **much, far, a lot, a great deal, a bit, slightly**: *much better, far more expensive.* Нельзя: ~~very better~~, ~~absolutely better~~. Строго говоря, предельные не сравнивают (*more perfect*), заменяя на *nearly perfect, closer to perfect.*

## Устойчивые «усилители»
Некоторые усилители привязаны к определённым прилагательным (коллокации):
*bitterly cold, deeply moved / ashamed, highly unlikely / effective, fully aware, perfectly clear, utterly ridiculous, downright dangerous, deadly serious / dead serious, fast / sound asleep, wide awake, stark naked.*

## Двойная природа
У некоторых слов значение определяет градуируемость. *Different*: *very different* (градуируемое), *completely different* (предельное). *Right*: *quite right* (предельное), но *very right* — нет.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~She was very furious.~~ → She was **absolutely furious.** (или *very angry*)
- ~~The soup is absolutely cold.~~ → The soup is **stone cold.** / **very** cold.
- ~~a very wooden spoon~~ → **a wooden spoon**
- ~~The task was nearly good.~~ → The task was **fairly** good.
en:
## Gradable and ungradable
**Gradable** adjectives describe a quality that can be measured on a scale: *good, tired, cold, old, expensive*. They go with *very, extremely, fairly, rather, quite, a bit* and the comparative.
**Ungradable** adjectives are of three kinds:
1. **Extreme:** the meaning already includes "very". *enormous* (= very big), *terrible, fantastic, exhausted, freezing, furious, delighted, brilliant, awful, hilarious, starving, tiny, ancient.*
2. **Absolute / limit:** the state is either true or not. *perfect, impossible, essential, unique, dead, identical, unanimous, right.*
3. **Classifying:** they put a thing in a category. *wooden, nuclear, medical, British, daily, electric, annual.*

## Choosing the intensifier
| Type | Use | Do not use |
|---|---|---|
| Gradable | very, extremely, really, fairly, pretty, rather, quite, a bit | ~~absolutely good~~ |
| Extreme / absolute | **absolutely, utterly, completely, totally, really** | ~~very exhausted~~, ~~very impossible~~ |
| Absolute (nearly) | **almost, nearly, virtually, practically** | |
> The view was **absolutely breathtaking**, but I was only **very tired**.
> It is **virtually impossible** to find a parking space here.
- ~~very fantastic~~ → **absolutely** fantastic / **really** fantastic
- ~~absolutely tired~~ → **very** tired / **absolutely exhausted**
- ~~very impossible~~ → **almost** impossible / **absolutely** impossible
**really** is the universal one: *really good* and *really fantastic* are both fine.

## The special case of quite
British *quite* has **two meanings**:
- with gradable adjectives = "fairly, moderately": *quite good* (= fairly good, not great);
- with extreme and absolute adjectives = "completely": *quite impossible, quite perfect, quite right.*
Americans often use *quite* like *very*. *Rather* is similar to *quite* but often suggests surprise or complaint: *rather expensive, rather good (I didn't expect it).*

## Comparatives
To strengthen a comparative use **much, far, a lot, a great deal, a bit, slightly**: *much better, far more expensive.* Not ~~very better~~ or ~~absolutely better~~. Strictly speaking, absolute adjectives are not compared (*more perfect*); we say *nearly perfect*.

## Collocations
Some intensifiers are tied to certain adjectives:
*bitterly cold, deeply moved / ashamed, highly unlikely / effective, fully aware, perfectly clear, utterly ridiculous, downright dangerous, deadly serious / dead serious, fast / sound asleep, wide awake, stark naked.*

## Words with a double nature
For some words, meaning decides. *Different*: *very different* (gradable), *completely different* (absolute). *Right*: *quite right* (absolute), but not *very right*.

## Common mistakes
- ~~She was very furious.~~ → She was **absolutely furious.** (or *very angry*)
- ~~The soup is absolutely cold.~~ → The soup is **stone cold.** / **very** cold.
- ~~a very wooden spoon~~ → **a wooden spoon**
structure:
## Типы прилагательных
| Тип | Примеры | Усилитель |
|---|---|---|
| градуируемые | good, tired, cold, expensive | very, extremely, fairly, rather |
| крайние | enormous, exhausted, freezing, fantastic | absolutely, utterly, completely |
| предельные | perfect, impossible, essential, unique | absolutely, completely, almost |
| классифицирующие | wooden, nuclear, British, medical | — |

## Усилители
| Слово | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| very / extremely / really | градуируемые: «очень» | very tired |
| absolutely / utterly / totally | крайние и предельные: «совершенно» | absolutely exhausted |
| almost / nearly / virtually | предельные: «почти» | almost impossible |
| quite (BrE) | gradable: «довольно»; extreme / absolute: «совсем» | quite good · quite perfect |
| much / far / a lot | сравнительная степень | much better |

## Сильные пары
| Сочетание | Значение |
|---|---|
| bitterly cold | очень холодно |
| deeply moved | глубоко тронут |
| highly unlikely | крайне маловероятно |
| fully aware | прекрасно сознаёт |
| perfectly clear | абсолютно ясно |
| fast / sound asleep | крепко спит |

exercises.title: very или absolutely?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте **very** или **absolutely** (иногда допустимы синонимы). В последнем пункте нужно слово со значением «почти».

items.text: The view from the top was {{absolutely|utterly|totally|completely|really}} breathtaking.
I was {{very|really|extremely}} tired after the long walk.
It is {{absolutely|totally|completely|really}} essential to book early.
She was {{very|really|extremely}} upset when she heard the news.
We were {{absolutely|totally|completely|really}} starving after the hike.
It's {{almost|nearly|virtually|practically}} impossible to find a parking space here.

exercises.example: The room was (very / absolutely) enormous. → The room was **absolutely** enormous.

exercises.title: Устойчивые усилители
exercises.instruction: Вставьте подходящее слово: bitterly, highly, fully, perfectly, deeply, fast, utterly, dead.

items.text: It was {{bitterly}} cold that night, and the wind never stopped.
It is {{highly}} unlikely that she will resign.
I'm {{fully|perfectly|well}} aware of the risks involved.
He was {{deeply}} moved by the speech.

items.q: He was ___ tired after the flight.
The test was ___ impossible; hardly anyone passed.
My brother is ___ taller than me.

items.why: *Right* — предельное: **absolutely right** (в британском английском также *quite right*); *very right* и *rather right* не говорят.
*Cold* градуируемое, нужно *very cold*; *freezing* — крайнее и сочетается с *absolutely*.

items.q: В британском английском «The film was quite good» значит:
Что значит quite в «What you're asking is quite impossible»?
This phone is ___ more expensive than mine.
items.why: Сравнительную степень усиливают *much / far / a lot*: **far more expensive**.
Предельные прилагательные сочетаются с *almost / nearly*: **almost perfect**.

exercises.title: Усильте
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение: замените выделенную пару «very + прилагательное» на крайнее прилагательное с **absolutely**.

exercises.title: Переведите на английский
exercises.instruction: Переведите на английский. Ключевые слова даны.

answers: She is much cleverer than me.
She is much cleverer than I am.
She's much cleverer than I am.
She is much more clever than me.
She's much more clever than me.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Закончите предложения подходящим усилителем и прилагательным. Образцы — для самопроверки.

items.prompt: Опишите вашу последнюю поездку: The trip was absolutely ...
Опишите, как вы чувствуете себя после рабочего дня: After work I'm usually very ...
items.sample: After work I'm usually very tired.

items.prompt: Что для вас практически невозможно? (virtually impossible)
items.sample: It's virtually impossible for me to get up before six.

items.prompt: Расскажите о погоде в вашем городе зимой (bitterly cold / freezing).
items.sample: In January it's bitterly cold, and sometimes it's absolutely freezing.

items.prompt: Напишите, что вы считаете совершенно необходимым в вашей жизни (absolutely essential).
items.sample: Good friends are absolutely essential for me.
